$comment: #NEW-145 / #NEW-143 D4 (Danny 2026-11-26): MCP TASKS on Exponential's MCP server, the `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks` extension (tasks.extensions.modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28), UNIFIED with the session watches (#NEW-49): an MCP task is the second kind of WATCHER on `session_watches` (packages/eagent fixtures/rules.json `watcher`, kind `watcherKind`), next to a session; ONE system, not two. ROW (server-side, #NEW-147): `mcp_tasks` {id = the taskId (`tsk_` + 32 random bytes base64url: unguessable), principal (`user:<id>|client:<oauth client id or token prefix>`, elicitation.json's), status, status_message, cards (the open cards it renders, by message id), result, error, created_at, last_updated_at, expires_at = created_at + `ttlMs`}; `session_watches` gains `watcher_kind` (`session` | `mcp_task`, default `session`) and `task_id`; a task watcher's `session_id` is null. WHO GETS ONE (`taskWatchFor`, `eligibilityCases`): only a `tool` call (`exponential_sessions_send`) from an EXTERNAL caller (not inside a session of its own: our own agents keep wake messages) whose request's `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities"].extensions` declared the extension, while it holds fewer than `maxLivePerPrincipal` live tasks; past it, or for anyone else, the call answers as today. The server decides, the client never asks (no request field). What it watches, first match: a message to `sessionId` or `agentId` (the agent's conversation) = that session; a start (`text`, `promptId` or `issueIds`, no target) = the started session; else a `wakeOn` of EVENT specs only (`eventSpecPattern`: `pr:N`, `pr:N:closed`, `issue:X[:status]`, `at:<ISO>`) = those events (one task, all its watches). A stop or an answer never makes a task. The call's ordinary work happens first; its result is then the CreateTaskResult = the Task (`taskWire`) + `resultType` "task", returned only once tasks/get would find it. STATUS MAPPING (`taskReduce`, `reduceCases`; the bus that posts a `session` watcher's wake lines drives a task watcher instead, and never posts for it): a watched session's TRANSITION (any bus line about it) = `working`, `statusMessage` = the last non-blank line of its digest (`sessions.digest`), clipped to `statusMessageMax`; an OPEN ask or plan card = `input_required` with `inputRequests` keyed by the CARD MESSAGE ID (unique for the task's life, never reused), each an `elicitation/create` form (`cardRequest`, `cardCases`: an ask = `answer` oneOf its options (`answers` array anyOf when multi) plus a free `text` unless `custom` is false, or `text` alone without options; a plan = its text clipped to `planMax` (eagent rules.ask.planMax), `decision` approved/rejected plus `q_<id>` oneOf per question); a SEALED card cannot be rendered by the server: the task stays `working` with `copy.sealedCard` and the card is answered in the app; the card answered (by anyone: first wins) = back to `working` unless another card is open; the END REPORT = `completed`, `result` = a CallToolResult {content: [{type: text, text: the summary (empty = `copy.noSummary`)}], isError: false}; an end with a failure reason (`failures`: the device's stall watchdog (eagent rules.report.reasons.stalled), the watchdog or a person killing it, a failed start) = `failed`, `error` {code `failureCode`, message}; an EVENT watch FIRING (`watch.fire`, a `gone` subject included) = `completed` with the host's fire text as the result. A terminal task ignores everything after. Every change stamps `lastUpdatedAt`. METHODS (`taskHandle`, `handleCases`; over Streamable HTTP the Mcp-Name header = params.taskId): `tasks/get {taskId}` = the Task + `resultType` "complete"; `tasks/update {taskId, inputResponses}` = {resultType "complete"}; each response keyed by an OPEN card goes through CARD-ANSWER (`cardAnswer`, `sessions.send {sessionId, answer}`: first wins; accept = `answers` (the picked labels; a label not offered = nothing) or `answer` (the free text), a plan = `decision` + `answers` {id: [label]}; decline = `dismissed`; cancel = nothing, the card stays open); unknown, answered or sealed keys are ignored; the status moves when the bus reports the card answered (eventually consistent); `tasks/cancel {taskId}` = {resultType "complete"}: a live task turns `cancelled` (`copy.cancelled`), its watcher row goes, and a session task STOPS its session (`sessions.send {sessionId, stop: true}`: the turn is interrupted; the session itself stays, like any stopped session); cancelling a terminal task changes nothing. ERRORS (`errors`, `errorCodes`): a client that did not declare the extension = -32021 with data.requiredCapabilities (`missingCapability`); more than `rateLimit.max` tasks/* calls by one principal within `rateLimit.windowSeconds` (deletes.json's sliding window; clients poll at `pollIntervalMs`) = `rateLimited`; a missing taskId, an unknown one or ANOTHER PRINCIPAL'S (same answer: no leak) = -32602 `missingTaskId` / `notFound`; past `ttlMs` from creation = -32602 `expired` (the watcher row is gone at expiry; the session keeps running, it is an ordinary session); inputResponses not an object = -32602. No tasks/list (the spec has none). Times are unix ms in, ISO 8601 out. GENUI (#NEW-149, MCP Apps): when the watched session posted a SURFACE card (`exponential_show` with a surface, kind `surface`), its end report's result also carries that card for the host's genUI view: `structuredContent` = {shown: "inline", card: {kind: "surface", surface, title}} (the LAST surface card it posted; the inline show's answer, packages/mcp-apps genui/result.ts) and `_meta.ui.resourceUri` = `genuiResourceUri`; the text content stays the summary. A failure or an event firing never carries one. TRANSFERS (#FEED-295, Danny 2026-11-27: a transfer's end reaches an outside host as an MCP task, never a push notification): `exponential_transfers_write {op: send}` (`transferTool`) from an EXTERNAL caller that declared the extension also gets a task, watching that TRANSFER (`watch` `transfer`, `transferId`; under `maxLivePerPrincipal` like any task); its other ops (cancel) never make one, and our own agents keep their wake line. The transfer's progress = `working`, `statusMessage` = `copy.transferProgress` (sizes in decimal units B, KB, MB, GB, TB with one decimal under 100); its end = `completed` with the end line as the result (`done`), `failed` with `error` {code `failureCode`, message = the end line} (`failed`), or `cancelled` with the end line (`cancelled`). `tasks/cancel` on a live transfer task CANCELS THE TRANSFER (effect `cancel_transfer`: both machines stop, what arrived stays; `copy.transferCancelled`).
